title: Add a title and a transition
summary: Put a Text Plus title over your video and blend two clips with a Cross Dissolve.

steps.say: Click Edit on the bottom bar of the window to open the Edit page.

checks.prompt: Is the Edit page active, with the Edit icon highlighted on the bottom bar and a timeline across the lower part of the window?

hints: The page buttons are icons with labels in a row along the very bottom edge. Edit is one of them.
You can also press Shift 4 to jump straight to the Edit page.
steps.why: Every task in Resolve belongs to a page, and the Edit page has the tools for this lesson.

steps.say: Click Effects near the top left of the window to open the Effects panel.

check.prompt: Is the Effects panel open on the left, showing a Toolbox list with Video Transitions and Titles?

hints: Effects is a button in the toolbar under the menu bar, next to Media Pool.
In older versions the button is called Effects Library.
steps.why: The Effects panel holds the ready-made titles and transitions.

steps.say: In the Toolbox list, click Titles, then find Text Plus under Fusion Titles.

check.prompt: Is the Titles list showing in the Effects panel, with a Text+ entry visible?

hints: Text Plus appears as Text with a plus sign. Scroll down past the basic titles to Fusion Titles.
Type Text into the search box at the top of the Effects panel to filter the list.
steps.why: Text Plus gives you more styling options than the basic Text title.

steps.say: Drag Text Plus onto the empty track above your clip in the timeline.

checks.prompt: Is there a new title clip on a video track above the other clips?

hints: Drop it on track V2, above your video, so the text shows on top of the picture.
If there is no empty track, drop it above the top track and Resolve adds one.
steps.why: Clips on higher tracks are drawn on top of the clips below them.

steps.say: Click the title clip, then click Inspector at the top right of the window.

check.prompt: Is the Inspector panel open on the right, showing text settings for the title?

hints: Inspector is the last button at the right end of the toolbar under the menu bar.
Double-clicking the title clip in the timeline also opens it in the Inspector.
steps.why: The Inspector is where you change the words, font, size and color.

steps.say: In the Inspector, click the Text box, delete the sample words, and type your title.

check.prompt: Does the viewer show the new title text over the video instead of the sample text?

hints: The Text box is at the top of the Inspector, under the Title tab.
Move the playhead over the title clip so the viewer shows it.
steps.why: Your own words replace the placeholder text in the title.

steps.say: In the Toolbox list, click Video Transitions, then drag Cross Dissolve onto the cut between two clips.

checks.prompt: Is there a transition marker sitting across the join between two clips on the timeline?

hints: Drop it right on the line where one clip ends and the next one starts.
Or click that join and press Control T, which adds the default Cross Dissolve.
steps.why: A dissolve fades one shot into the next so the change feels smooth.

steps.say: Move the playhead before the transition and press Space to watch it.

checks.prompt: Is the video playing in the timeline viewer?

hints: Click in the time ruler a little to the left of the join, then press Space.
Press Space again to stop playback.
steps.why: Watching the result tells you whether the title and dissolve last long enough.
